page: Amazon Web Services r6i.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per physical core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but offers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with the server achieving top-tier ratings in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions and encryption. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 338.62 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations. In database and caching workloads, the server demonstrates high throughput, processing 111.87 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall within the average range, while ray tracing and image processing tasks perform in the top tier.

Given its bare-metal architecture and massive memory capacity, this server offers high resource density for enterprise workloads. The absence of local storage means storage-heavy applications must rely on network-attached options, which is a key architectural tradeoff. The server is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and multi-threaded enterprise workloads that benefit from dedicated physical hardware access.
